page.layout: One printed page, cut off at the right, so only its left part is on this scan. Down the page, from top to bottom: a large display capital "A" with a smaller line beside it, a short line with "W" below it, a line beginning "M. V", a line beginning "VV" at the left, and at the bottom a line of Roman numerals beginning "III". No margins and no notes.; One page of large display capitals, set in a single column, with the lines printed upside down. Only the right part of the page is visible.; One title-page fragment, the left part of the page, with large capitals in several lines and smaller lines below them. Mirrored show-through from the other side appears in the lower half.
page.notes: The scan shows only faint, mostly faded fragments of large display letters at the left. Nearly all the text is illegible. The letters read here are guesses from their shapes. The line at the bottom may be a Roman numeral, but I cannot be sure of it. Nothing else is legible on this part. The lines are printed upside down and the letters are partly cut off at the left edge, so the words are fragmentary. Readings marked [?] are uncertain. The line beginning "IVM AC" may be "JVM AC" or similar; the word after "EI" is uncertain. Several of the lines are very broad capitals, and their letter spacing is hard to judge. The page is cut off at the left and right, so most lines are fragments. The small lines in the middle and lower half look mirrored, which indicates show-through from the reverse side; I have not transcribed them as printed text beyond the few readable fragments. The large capitals are only partly legible. The dark marks beside "LEON" are ink spots, not text.
